description.narrative: (USAID Global Health (GH)): EngageHCD is a contracting vehicle available to USAID's Bureau for Global Health and Missions to procure technical assistance on state-of-the-art human-centered design (HCD) services and explore how to scale up activities to encourage uptake and adherence to care seeking behavior. HCD is a discipline that applies a specific mindset and skill set for creative problem solving by placing the values, needs, and behavior of people at the center of our work. HCD approaches leverages design thinking expertise to generate insights, co-create prototypes, test options, and iterate solutions hand-in-hand with the target end-users. There are a range of specializations within design, such as experience design, service delivery design, communication design, and product design. HCD is used to develop informed, inclusive, purposeful, compelling, and innovative solutions that better fit into people's lives as well as into the broader systems that they live in. Examples of this work include driving demand for the use of chlorhexidine to increase newborn health and increasing the uptake of the dapivirine ring (DPV ring) for HIV prevention. HCD expertise is used to support the development and adaptation of tools to encourage uptake and correct use of the DPV ring-and other rings in the pipeline-among young women by situating its use within their daily values, needs, and lives. HCD is also being used to adapt and pilot an oral PrEP campaign that reframes oral PrEP from a medical product to a fashion or beauty product that can easily fit into a young woman's daily ritual. In another effort, HCD is being used to explore the potential of alternative private sector channels for PrEP, driven by the needs of the end users and pain points they experience with current offerings.
